content: DOM-based Extension Clickjacking (Marek Toth, DEF CON 33 / Aug 2025): 11 major password-manager extensions (1Password, Bitwarden, Enpass, LastPass, LogMeOnce, RoboForm, NordPass, ProtonPass, Dashlane, Keeper, iCloud Passwords) were all vulnerable in default config. Attack chains opacity:0/0.001 on the extension's injected DOM root or Popover, focus()-chaining onto hidden autofill-triggering inputs, and z-index/pointer-events:none overlays so a user's visible click (e.g. on a fake cookie banner) actually lands on a hidden credential-autofill trigger. Closed shadow-root gave only PARTIAL protection -- child elements were still opacity-modifiable once an attacker found the root element; ProtonPass stayed exploitable after its first fix because the shadow-root element name just needed re-discovery per page load. Recommended mitigations: MutationObserver to detect/block style tampering, occlusion detection via elementsFromPoint(), verifying top-layer state before rendering, and -- the strongest recommendation -- using a SYSTEM-LEVEL / browser-chrome dialog instead of any DOM-injected element. Researcher's own conclusion: 'no simple protection exists' at the in-page application level; robust defense needs browser-level API support.
